messages:
alex: saw recurring intermittent packet loss on overlay during nightly inference bursts. endpoints in pod-to-pod e2e ping show 0.5-2% loss for ~30s windows, then clears. correlates with heavy KV cache fetches from redis + big embeddings uploads.
cheng: which cluster/region? node names? any k8s events?
alex: prod-gpu-us-west-2, nodes gpu-w-13,gpu-w-17,gpu-w-21. No crashloop events. kube-proxy logs show occasional conntrack GC spikes at same times.
samir: do we have netdev/XDP drops? can you drop the BPF counters?
alex: net-monitor-bot attached XDP counters snapshot: XDP_DROP went up ~380 over 2 mins on gpu-w-17, netdev backlog spikes visible. Also saw `NET_RX_OVERRUN` increments in dmesg on that host.
irene: pulled tcpdump on host egress during a window, sample: `16:42:12.123456 IP podA > podB: UDP, length 1380` repeated, then bursts of no replies. also saw fragmented large encapsulated packets hitting MTU boundary: `DF set, frag needed and DF set`.
oncall-bernie: interesting — we run VXLAN (geneve mode) with outer UDP. jumbo frames? MTU configured to 9000 at host and mtu in CNI is 8950. Any GSO/GRO offload toggles?
alex: hosts have ethtool showing gso/gro on. tried toggling `ethtool -K eth0 gso off` on a test node which reduced packet loss spikes but cpu for host networking shot up ~12%.
samir: that suggests host-side encapsulation+large GSO sizes are creating oversized UDP packets that get dropped at NIC or switch when buffers overflow. Also Mellanox drivers historically have edge cases with large GSO + VXLAN. firmware?
alex: mlx5 driver 5.14.21 + fw 14.25 applied 2 months ago.
cheng: what about net.core.netdev_max_backlog and rmem/wmem? current netdev_max_backlog is 1000. can you bump it and test?
irene: also saw qdisc tx_queue length thrashing in `/sys/class/net/eth0/tx_queue_len` during the burst. tried `sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=50000` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.udp_mem='281857 375809 563648'` on a test node — backlog stabilized and loss dropped to ~0.2% but not zero.
oncall-bernie: any signs of hardware offload for vxlan? `ethtool -k` shows rx-vlan-offload is on but vxlan offload is driver-dependent.
samir: we should test two orthogonal mitigations: 1) force smaller GSO segmentation by `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=...` (not relevant) — better: `sysctl -w net.core.gso_max_size=1220` (kernel option) to reduce composite packet sizes; 2) tune CNI to enable host-gw mode for heavy cross-node KV traffic (avoid double-encap).
alex: ran `echo 1220 > /proc/sys/net/core/gso_max_size` on test node — big drop in CPU for re-transmission but increased packet count. CPU went up ~6% but NV network CPU stayed within SLA. loss reduced to ~0.05% during a 10m test.
cheng: can we reproduce reliably? any correlation with particular p95 inference latencies?
irene: yes, p95 inference latency spikes aligned with the short loss windows. likely large backend responses cause sudden egress bursts.
oncall-bernie: immediate action plan: 1) roll gso_max_size change to canary subset of gpu nodes tonight; 2) increase netdev_max_backlog cluster-wide via daemonset for short-term; 3) schedule mlx5 firmware + driver bump with perf testing next week; 4) examine CNI per-route for redis traffic to avoid overlay where possible.
samir: long-term: work with NIC vendor to validate VXLAN offload path or migrate heavy intra-node flows to hostnetworked sidecars or use SR-IOV on critical nodes. Also add additional monitoring: expose GSO/GRO counters, netdev backlog metric, and an alert when XDP_DROP > 50/min.
alex: implemented canary changes on gpu-w-13,gpu-w-17 with gso_max_size=1220 + netdev_max_backlog=50000 and will monitor. adding throttle in the inference client to smooth bursts as quick mitigation.
net-monitor-bot: alert suppressed: overlay-loss-window gpu-w-17 cleared :white_check_mark: (was 1768003512 -> 1768003578)
cheng: thanks — keep updates here. if the canary behaves, we’ll roll to prod by 0500 UTC. :eyes:
